description: The exact configuration of the one-shot locked-test benchmark. Every setting is explicit; nothing is 'auto', 'latest' or free. Derived from stage_b_frozen_v1 plus the Stage C selection decisions. Sealed by a manifest of sha256 pins; run_experiment refuses to run on any drift, and the holdout is one-shot (locked_benchmark_run_state.json).

stage_c.note: Stage C results are immutable inputs to this freeze; nothing here re-derives or edits them.

split.cases: the whole locked test split, every case, in stored (sorted case id) order; no subset
split.case_count_source: data/eval/splits/split_manifest_v1.json overall_counts.test (pre-existing manifest metadata; no test id is read to freeze)
split.decision_time: as_of = the case's own created_date (T0, ticket-only)

graph.note: checked live before the run starts

issue_category.state_projection: issue_category_state: ticket, customer tier/industry/size, reported product, visible signal count and types
issue_category.runtime_status: supporting_signal: stable and calibrated, with a validation automation region; the LLM ties it on accuracy, so its value is cost, latency and calibrated deferral
issue_category.reason: Generalization confirmed on validation (73.0% to 78.4%, ECE 0.030), cheap to measure, and a frozen automation threshold exists that has not yet been tested on unseen data.

root_cause.state_projection: root_cause_state at v4_operational: ticket, reported product, deployed components, technical evidence, operational events
root_cause.runtime_status: supporting_only: degraded from dev (48.0% to 37.2%) and abstains with RC40 on 40% of decisions; usable only with human review
root_cause.reason: Scientific completeness, not a deployment claim: it re-tests once on unseen data whether the Jev lead over the LLM (+16.5 points on validation) holds, and whether the dev-to-validation drop repeats.

standard.reason: no grid threshold met observed error <= 5%, Wilson upper bound <= 10% and >= 50 automated decisions on validation

strict.reason: no grid threshold met observed error <= 2%, Wilson upper bound <= 4% and >= 50 automated decisions on validation

causal_change.state_projection: causal_change_state: ticket, reported product, deployed components, technical evidence (changes and deployments are offered only as candidates)
causal_change.runtime_status: runtime_candidate_conditional: conditional on the locked result; two qualifiers travel with it (JEV-028: 41% of decisions are trivially determined by candidate generation; JEV-025: the change-id artifact is unresolved on validation)
causal_change.reason: The only primitive to clear the pre-registered Stage C rubric: 89.3% [87.2, 91.6] against a 71.3% evidence-blind rule, stable against dev, 0.4% false-confident, candidate recall 100%.

threshold_selection.population_definition: decisions that offered at least one real change (decisions offering only `none` are resolved by candidate generation and excluded)

strict.reason: no grid threshold met observed error <= 2%, Wilson upper bound <= 4% and >= 50 automated decisions on validation

owning_team.state_projection: owning_team_state: ticket, reported product, deployed components, evidence summary
owning_team.runtime_status: supporting_only: generalizes and is far ahead of the LLM, but 37.6% primary accuracy and 5.3% false-confident; a routing suggestion with human confirmation at most
owning_team.reason: Scientific completeness: candidate coverage (99.7% to 99.9%) and the Jev lead over the LLM (+23.1 points) generalized on validation and are re-tested once on unseen data.

standard.reason: no grid threshold met observed error <= 5%, Wilson upper bound <= 10% and >= 50 automated decisions on validation

strict.reason: no grid threshold met observed error <= 2%, Wilson upper bound <= 4% and >= 50 automated decisions on validation

evidence_sufficiency.state_projection: evidence_sufficiency_state with the time-gated observable telemetry-anomaly summary (evidence_sufficiency_v2)
evidence_sufficiency.reason: 12.4% against a 92.9% majority baseline on validation (the LLM, 41.9%, is also below it). Excluded so the untouched test data stay available to any redesigned version; another measurement of this version would add little.

incident_relationship.candidate_strategy: active_incidents_overlapping_case (one Noul question per overlapping incident)
incident_relationship.state_projection: incident_relationship_state: ticket, reported product, case signal count, candidate incident
incident_relationship.runtime_status: deprioritize (borderline insufficient evidence: the sample is interpretable but cannot separate Jev from the baseline)
incident_relationship.reason: 82.6% against a 78.0% 'never related' baseline (lower bound below it); Jev found 8 of 29 related incidents. Excluded to preserve untouched data for a redesign that supplies more true-related incidents.

context_version_note: context_version is a root-cause-only setting; every other decision ignores it.

jev.note: Pinned to the explicit version id (accepted by the API and resolving identically to the jev-latest alias on 2026-09-23); the alias is not used.

confidence.jev: the API `confidence` field as delivered (JEV-032: not the probability of the chosen option)
confidence.llm: the self-reported confidence the model writes (a coarse number with few distinct values)
confidence.comparability: not comparable across systems; calibration is reported per system and never ranked against the other

orchestration.note: Workers change scheduling, not inputs: each decision's input is built once and sent to both systems. Latencies are therefore measured under 8-way concurrency, as in Stage C.

run.name: locked_benchmark_run
run.command: python3 -m agent.jev_v2.run_experiment --name locked_benchmark_run --kind locked_benchmark --split test --compare-llm --frozen-config locked_benchmark_frozen_v1
run.resume: only of the same run name under the same configuration, and only to complete cases that did not finish; completed cases are never re-sent

statistics.difference_vs_validation: Newcombe hybrid-score 95% interval for two independent proportions (locked minus validation)
statistics.jev_vs_llm: paired by (case, decision, incident) on identical inputs verified by hash; exact two-sided McNemar test; paired bootstrap 95% interval of the accuracy difference
statistics.reading_labels: material degradation / plausible sampling variation / improvement / insufficient sample (either side under 30); no fixed percentage threshold; interval-based only
statistics.multiplicity: no adjustment; p-values are reported unadjusted and marginal values are not interpreted

analysis.slice_rules: a slice under 30 decisions is marked small; a slice is flagged 'confidence does not track accuracy' when it has >= 30 decisions and (mean confidence - accuracy) exceeds the overall value by >= 0.10
analysis.candidate_size_bins: each distinct size when there are six or fewer distinct sizes, otherwise terciles of the locked distribution; empty bins are dropped

causal_recency_groups.A: true change is the newest candidate
causal_recency_groups.B: true change is visible and strictly older than another candidate (ties count as A)
causal_recency_groups.D: two or more real candidates offered (cuts across A/B/C)

analysis.failure_categories: invalid output or API error; candidate missing; wrong at confidence >= 0.90; wrong at lower confidence; correct at confidence < 0.50; correct otherwise (+ causal, incident, sufficiency sub-categories as in Stage C)

capability_rubric.T1: lower 95% bound of accuracy above the best evidence-blind rule
capability_rubric.T2: no material degradation against validation and candidate recall >= 0.95 (owning team judged on acceptable recall)
capability_rubric.headline: owning team is read on PRIMARY-team accuracy, as in Stage C (acceptable accuracy is the pre-registered primary metric of the report, reported alongside)

analysis.exploratory_rule: any analysis not listed in the protocol is exploratory and must be labelled as such; none may be a headline

threshold_policy.text: see agent/jev_v2/threshold_policy.py (pinned) and the protocol; thresholds below in each decision's threshold_selection are FIXED and are only evaluated, never re-selected, on the locked run

cost_accounting.tokens: provider-returned usage summed over every attempt
cost_accounting.llm_price_note: ASSUMPTION: the Together pricing page lists no separate Turbo row for the Llama 3.3 70B model id; the Llama 3.3 70B serverless price is applied
cost_accounting.reported: cost per decision and per 1,000 decisions, per decision type

latency.measure: client-side wall-clock milliseconds per request as recorded in each decision record

one_shot.rule: written before the first call; afterwards only --resume of the same run under the same configuration is accepted; any change to this file or any pinned file invalidates the run as a holdout benchmark

rationale.inclusion: Inclusion in the locked test (measure once on the final holdout) is separate from runtime candidacy. Evidence sufficiency and incident relationship are excluded to keep untouched data for possible redesigns.
rationale.causal_key_mode: canonical, the validated configuration. JEV-025 (change-id artifact) is unresolved on validation; switching to opaque keys would run an unvalidated configuration. If the opaque control on validation shows reliance, a new freeze version (opaque keys) is required before any locked run.
rationale.workers: 8, as in Stage C, so latency is measured under the same conditions.
rationale.thresholds: selected on validation by a versioned policy that never relaxes itself; root cause and owning team have none because no grid threshold came near the policy.
